title: Quota enforcer shard reconciliation to stop soft 429 cascades
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Summary:
On 2026-02-25 we observed a progressive increase in soft 429s across several small-tenant API keys during a regional capacity fluctuation window. The immediate symptom was elevated 429s for short-lived, high-burst requests while larger tenants were unaffected. Postmortem analysis shows the quota-enforcer's shard lease renewal and local count reconciliation diverged under two conditions: (1) transient node restarts during a rolling infra upgrade and (2) regional clock skew causing some leases to appear expired to other nodes. The divergence produced a window where two shards believed they owned overlapping token ranges, leading to double-counting in enforcement preferring local caches and ultimately rejecting legitimate requests as over-quota (soft 429s).

Root cause:
- Race in shard lease renewal: renewLease() path did not guarantee atomic visibility in central metadata when renewal happened concurrently with a node reclaim.
- No periodic cross-shard reconciliation: no small-window repair job existed to detect and correct overlapping token counts or orphaned leases.
- Insufficient instrumentation for lease transitions: dashboards showed only lease counts and not delta over time, making early detection difficult.

Work completed so far:
- Identified failing code paths and created a patch that adds an idempotent renewal handshake (PR linked below). Patch ensures renewals write both lease TTL and sequence epoch in a single atomic update.
- Implemented a lightweight reconciliation job that runs every 30s on the control plane to detect overlapping leases and emit repair ops to tombstone orphaned shards. Initially deployed to canary region us-west-2.
- Added metrics: lease_epoch, lease_renew_latency, overlapping_shard_count and a Grafana dashboard panel for rapid correlation with 429-rate.
- Performed synthetic replay load test that reproduced soft-429 pattern and validated the reconciliation job reduces overlap to zero in <120s.

Planned rollout and mitigation:
- Short term: enable reconciliation job globally behind a feature flag; increase lease TTL from 15s to 30s to reduce churn during rolling restarts. Will monitor for increased latency in reclaims.
- Medium term: merge idempotent-renew PR and retire non-atomic renewal path; add a distributed test harness for lease racing scenarios.
- Long term: introduce an event-sourced audit log for quota-enforcer state transitions and a reconciliation sanity check during during deployments (preflight).

Links and artifacts:
- Initial incident timeline & notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/INC-2026-02-25-quota-enforcer
- Github PR (reconciliation + atomic-renew changes): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1287
- Follow-up PR (reuse audit-indexing): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1310
- Load test harness and reproducer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/main/tools/quota-repro
- Incident dashboard (Grafana panels): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/5IhquX/quota-enforcer-incident
- Pager duty incident: PD-74321

Notes about risk/tradeoffs:
- Increasing lease TTL reduces churn during upgrades but slightly delays failover for truly dead nodes; mitigation: add faster explicit heartbeat on controlled reclaims.
- Reconciliation job writes tombstone repairs to central metadata; must be conservative to avoid deleting legitimately active leases — job currently requires 3 consecutive overlapping observations before repair.

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Reconciliation job running globally behind flag with monitoring and runbook entries.
- Non-atomic renewal path removed and replaced by idempotent-renew with tests.
- Automated end-to-end test that injects clock skew reproduces the prior soft-429 pattern and verifies fix.
